Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 Four employees and two companies, including Distrigaz, indicted in Rahova apartment block explosion case Category: English Date: 2026-11-04 17:18:44 Foto: Grigore POPESCU / AGERPRES Photo The Prosecutor's Office attached to the Bucharest Court of Appeal has indicted four employees and two companies, including gas distributor Distrigaz, on charges of negligent destruction resulting in a disaster in connection with an October 2025 apartment block explosion in Bucharest's Rahova district that killed four people. The defendants include two Distrigaz emergency-response technicians and two employees of Amproperty Construct SRL, a company authorized to perform inspections and technical reviews of gas installations. Distrigaz and Amproperty Construct have also been charged as legal entities. A total of 297 individuals and entities have joined the case as civil parties. To secure potential damages, prosecutors froze assets worth up to EUR 68.1 million and RON 6.55 million. Among the assets seized is Distrigaz's headquarters property, with the total value of frozen assets exceeding EUR 68 million. The explosion that occurred on Oct. 17, 2025 at a residential building in Sector 5 killed four people, injured eight and rendered uninhabitable all 54 apartments in the affected stairwell; also, 96 apartments in neighboring sections were damaged and 45 vehicles were destroyed or damaged. According to the indictment, an underground polyethylene gas pipe supplying the building was perforated at two points on Oct. 16 due to the heat generated by faults in underground electrical cables. Gas escaped into the soil, migrated through an underground utility corridor to the building's basement and spread through the elevator shaft and technical ducts. The accumulation of gas created an explosive atmosphere that ignited at 9:08 a.m. on Oct. 17, most likely from a spark generated by an electrical switch in a fifth-floor apartment. Prosecutors said all six defendants failed to take the necessary measures to identify the source of the leak, isolate the damaged section and prevent gas accumulation, despite repeated warnings. Between Oct. 16 and Oct. 17, Distrigaz received seven reports of gas odors at the affected buildings. Prosecutors allege serious deficiencies in the company's emergency response, including inadequate inspections, failure to deploy sufficient resources, premature closure of incidents without identifying the fault, and failure to link repeated complaints into a single risk assessment. The two Distrigaz technicians are accused of conducting incomplete checks and failing to investigate the distribution network and neighboring basements despite signs of methane presence. Prosecutors noted that one technician closed and sealed a neighboring building's gas supply without expanding inspections, even after gas odors and alarms reappeared. Amproperty Construct and its two employees intervened at the building on Oct. 16 under a technical inspection contract concluded after the gas supply had been shut off. Although they detected gas in common areas, prosecutors say they failed to extend inspections to likely infiltration zones, notify the distributor, ensure ventilation or maintain safety measures before leaving the site more than 16 hours before the explosion. Prosecutors stressed that the installers are not accused of failing to repair the underground pipe, a responsibility that belonged to Distrigaz, but of failing to report the leak and maintain protective measures required under safety regulations. All defendants are charged with negligence, prosecutors arguing that, given their professional training and responsibilities, they should have foreseen the risk posed by an unlocated and unisolated gas leak in a residential building. The investigation, completed within a year of the explosion, involved more than 200 witness interviews, three major technical expert reports and extensive forensic examinations. Prosecutors dropped the case against electricity distributor Retele Electrice Romania, concluding that while an electrical fault caused the gas pipe to rupture, investigators found no breach of operational rules or evidence that the company could have foreseen the disaster. The case has been sent to Bucharest's Sector 5 Court.
